queue_transport_verified.scope: two real clients and a dedicated server; contention, capacity, exact charge/refund, claim race, owner redaction, historical recipe, legacy conversion, reconnect and normal restart
limits: Seeded fixture world (stoves, legacy jobs, historical queue record, materials, positions, world time written directly into a temp save); not human or natural play; two clients; one server process at a time.

Legacy single-job stoves are seeded into a current save-20 file and converted lazily by queue_cook over the network; migration of an actual pre-20 save file is not exercised here (schema suites cover it).

Request dedup: World receipts are keyed by server session nonce + peer + sequence and are not addressable by a client. The test replays the SAME Session sequence via Session.perform (counter rewound); it is dropped by Session's per-peer sequence gate before World. World-level receipt replay is not exercised over the network; disk receipts are checked to hold exactly one entry per successful action.
Contention is two clients against one single-threaded server; the race shows the serialized outcome only.
Server restart is a normal --quit-after stop + restart; no crash/kill or save-failure injection.
Reconnect uses fresh client processes after a clean exit, not a mid-request network drop.
No cooking UI, screenshots, material chest sourcing or other machines are exercised.
Plain ws:// on 127.0.0.1 only: no TLS/WSS, certificates, proxies, CDN or cloud hosting tested.
Unauthenticated room-key path only (register_player); the identity/ticket path (join_authenticated) is not exercised.
